title: Core Data Concepts
subtitle: The ideas behind every DP-900 question: data types, workloads and roles.

what.body: Before choosing any Azure service, you describe your data: how it is shaped, how apps use it, and who works with it. Get these three right and most DP-900 questions answer themselves.
what.example: An online store keeps orders in neat tables, product reviews as JSON, and product photos as image files — structured, semi-structured and unstructured data in one business.

concepts.body: Follows a fixed schema of rows and columns with defined types. Think SQL tables: CustomerID, Name, City. Easy to query, strict about shape.
Has organizational tags but no rigid table: JSON and XML with keys, arrays and nesting. Flexible when fields vary per record.
No predefined model at all: photos, videos, audio, PDFs. Stored as files/objects, not rows.
The blueprint: tables, columns, types, rules and relationships. Structured data always has one; semi-structured only hints at one.
Many small, fast operational writes and reads: placing orders, payments, updating stock. Optimized for speed per transaction.
Big scans over history to find trends: yearly revenue by region. Optimized for aggregations, not single rows.
A file just holds bytes. A database adds querying, indexing, transactions, security and recovery on top of storage.
Turns data into reports, dashboards and insights for decisions. Lives in Power BI.
Builds pipelines that ingest, transform and load data from sources into analytics platforms.
Keeps databases available, backed up, secure and fast: recovery, indexes, configuration.

examples.title: One store, three data types
examples.body: Orders table (structured), review JSON (semi-structured), product photo (unstructured).

examples.title: Spot the workload
examples.body: 'Charge this customer now' is OLTP. 'Which city grew fastest in 3 years?' is OLAP. Exam questions love this pair — look for time words like trends, history, aggregate.

comparisons.title: DBA vs Data Engineer vs Data Analyst
head: Role
Owns

services.name: Azure SQL Database
services.when: You need tables, schemas and SQL without managing servers.

services.name: Azure Cosmos DB
services.when: JSON data with global users and instant reads.
services.scenario: Reviews and catalogs served on every continent.

services.name: Azure Synapse Analytics
services.when: OLAP questions over years of data.

services.name: Azure Data Factory
services.when: Engineers must copy and transform on a schedule.
services.scenario: Nightly load of sales files into analytics.

remember: Structured = schema + rows/columns. JSON/XML = semi-structured. Media = unstructured.
Creating an order is transactional (OLTP); analyzing years of sales is analytical (OLAP).
DBA manages databases · Engineer builds pipelines · Analyst builds reports.
SQL Database = relational · Blob = unstructured files · Cosmos DB = global NoSQL · Synapse = analytics · Power BI = dashboards · Data Factory = pipelines.

quickCheck.q: A CSV of sales rows is…?
quickCheck.a: Structured (tabular) data — though a CSV file alone is not a database.

quickCheck.q: Recording 1,000 bank deposits: OLTP or OLAP?
Who tunes a slow query's indexes?
quickCheck.a: The DBA — performance and configuration are DBA duties.

quickCheck.q: Where do a million product photos belong?
quickCheck.a: Azure Blob Storage — object storage for unstructured files.

quickCheck.q: Why separate operational and analytical systems?
quickCheck.a: Different access patterns: tiny fast transactions vs huge aggregations.
